title: In Vitro Preparation of Actively Maturing Bovine Articular Cartilage Explants for X-Ray Phase Contrast Imaging
protocol: Prepare absorbent protector and a scalpel with #10 scalpel blade.
Spray all materials with 70% ethanol solution.
Soak the bovine leg to remove blood and mud.
Clean the leg with soap and scrub with a brush.
Spray the cleaned leg with 70% ethanol.
Place the leg on absorbent paper.
Cut around the feet with a scalpel.
Trace a delicate line along the length of the leg, taking extra care in the joint zone.
Remove the skin carefully along the scalpel line.
Put waste materials in a clinical waste bag.
Clean and brush the leg again after removing the skin.
Sterilize the cleaned leg with ethanol once more.
Do not damage the region close to the joint cavity.
If the joint cavity is opened or damaged, discard the leg.
Place the prepared leg in an Al-foil sprayed with 70% ethanol.
Place appropriately sized latex gloves over the ends of the leg to prevent blood egress from the proximal end or possible contamination from the hoof.
Dispose of waste materials in accordance with institutional rules.
Open the laminar flow hood 25 min before use.
Clean the laminar flow hood with alcohol 70%.
Warm culture medium in a water bath.
Prepare a 24 well plate with 1.5 mL of basic medium (DMEM-F12 only) in each well for washing.
Prepare another 24 well plate with 1.5 mL of complete culture medium in each well.
Store the prepared well plates in the culture incubator at 37 °C until use.
Place a universal tube containing 70% ethanol and another containing washing medium on a rack.
Place a scalpel and a 4 or 6-mm biopsy punch (initially placed in the alcohol universal tube) on the rack.
Transfer the tubes and materials under the hood.
Put an absorbent protector sprayed with 70% ethanol under the hood.
Prepare tissues that have been sprayed with 70% ethanol.
Cover a dissection plate with Al-foil.
Take previously prepared feet out of the refrigerator (4 °C) and spray them with 70% ethanol.
Dispose hazardous and clinical bags near the hood for autoclaving later.
Spray the foot with 70% ethanol.
Take the sterile scalpel.
Cut carefully along the midline of the joint following its contour.
Do not touch the metacarpophalangeal joint medial condyle cartilage.
Carefully cut the ligament when the joint is opened.
Throw away the lower part of the feet in an autoclave bag.
Remove all other tissues to expose the cartilage of the joint completely.
Place the scalpel and biopsy punch in alcohol, then in washing medium.
Make 4-5 circles with the biopsy punch along the internal faces of the bones.
Clean the bio-punch in alcohol after use.
Cut a line between each circle and along the central line of the bone with a scalpel.
To take out the cartilage explant, cut vertically on one border of the circle biopsy.
Carefully cut horizontally on the subchondral bone below the punch line to remove the explants.
Place the explant in a well plate filled with 1.5 mL of washing medium.
Perform experimental control and treatment of explants coming from the same location in the joint.
Check that the explant is well oriented correctly.
Ensure the surface of the explant faces up and the subchondral bone part faces the bottom of the well plate.
Keep the well plate closed between each biopsy.
Remove the washing medium.
Wash again with wash medium.
Leave in wash medium for 2-3 hours to allow blood and bone residues to flux out into the medium.
Transfer the explants into a new well plate containing complete culture medium carefully without touching anything with the pipette.
Check that explants are still correctly positioned (bone facing the bottom part of the well plate).
Clean everything and dispose of clinical waste in an appropriate place.
Change the explant culture medium every two days using warm fresh medium to sustain cell/tissue needs.
Wash the explants with DMEM-F12 under the tissue culture hood.
Wash the explants twice with PBS under the tissue culture hood.
Soak explants overnight at 4 °C in 10% NBFS (Neutral Buffer Formalin Saline).
Place the fixed explants in PBS in a microcentrifuge tube.
Store the explants at 4 °C.
Select conical plastic tips of an appropriate size for the sample and camera field of view.
Seal the cone tip with a flame to create a water-proof container.
Fill the sealed tip with PBS.
Insert the sample into the tip using tweezers.
Remove air bubbles by shaking slowly.
Mount the tube on the tomography stage.
Align the tube using simple radiographs.
Place the detector at 2.5 m from the sample.
Set the X-ray photon energy to 17 keV using a double Silicon crystal system in Bragg-Bragg geometry.
Mount an imaging detector consisting of a scientific CMOS camera with a 60 µm thick Gadolinium Oxysulfide scintillator screen on an optic for a resulting isotropic voxel size of 3.5 µm.
Acquire 2000 projections during a 360˚ scan of the sample with each projection exposed for 2 seconds.
Use a phase retrieval algorithm to extract the phase signal.
Set the ratio between the refraction and absorption index to 1,200 for optimal visualization of bone and cartilage.
Use a standard filtered back projection CT reconstruction algorithm.
Implement the PyHST2 code using an open-source, GPU-based version.
